seeds.title: Harden orchestrator auto-resolution determinism
seeds.statement: Define a deterministic Orchestrator auto-resolver matrix driven first by actor type and operation type, then scope and stack hints, with explicit fallback behavior.
evidence: The shard calls out that Orchestrator auto-resolver specifics are still too qualitative.
Recommended fix is a deterministic matrix by actor type, operation type, scope, and stack/domain hints, while keeping actor-type defaults stronger than stack hints.

seeds.title: Emit resolver reasoning metadata consistently
seeds.statement: Require each auto resolver to emit ranked candidates, selected winner, selection reason, and fallback reason whenever the preferred candidate is not effective.
evidence: The shard explicitly lists ranked candidate(s), winning candidate, and concise selection reason as required emissions.
It also requires fallback reason disclosure when preferred and effective candidates differ.

seeds.title: Preserve historical effective persona records
seeds.statement: Runtime history must preserve the resolved effective Persona and reason from execution time so historical views never recompute from current settings.
evidence: Do-not-forget notes require historical runs to preserve resolved effective Persona and reason.
Scoped override lifecycle concern emphasizes preventing leakage across run/task/subagent boundaries.

seeds.title: Keep review personas distinct from implementation
seeds.statement: Corroboration and review personas should remain distinct from original implementation personas to preserve independent governance and challenge roles.
evidence: The shard states corroboration/review personas should remain distinct from the original implementation persona whenever possible.
It also warns that weak actor-type mapping makes auto-selection feel arbitrary in overseer-heavy workflows.

seeds.title: Separate canonical terms from help copy
seeds.statement: Introduce a three-part help contract that keeps canonical term names stable while allowing Expert and ELI5 explanations to vary in phrasing only.
evidence: Recommended split distinguishes canonical term system, help entry system, and contextual help system.
Core principle says simple help should simplify explanation, not rename the model.

seeds.title: Define fixed template for concept help entries
seeds.statement: Concepts that are central to rewrite semantics should use a fixed help-entry template with definition, boundaries, related states/actions, and cross-links.
evidence: The shard recommends dedicated help entries for core concepts like Feature Seam, Work Package, Corroboration, Graph Patch, and concern lifecycle terms.
It proposes template fields including canonical name, short definition, why it matters, what it is not, related concepts, and surface examples.

seeds.title: Add related-concept linking across surfaces
seeds.statement: Help content should support explicit related-concept links so users can navigate coupled lifecycle concepts consistently across Settings, Orchestrator, History, and Ledger.
evidence: The shard explicitly recommends related-concept linking and gives multi-term clusters such as Promotion/Revoked/Reopened and Lane/Worktree/Cleanup states.
It notes exact records in History/Ledger should still offer concept help links for unfamiliar terms.

seeds.title: Use glossary as canonical concept inventory
seeds.statement: Treat Glossary as the canonical short-definition inventory and let richer help entries expand from that stable terminology base.
evidence: The shard states that Plans/Glossary.md should become the canonical concept inventory backbone.
It recommends a split where Glossary holds canonical short definitions and help entries provide fuller examples and links.

seeds.title: Constrain ELI5 to semantic equivalence
seeds.statement: Expert and ELI5 variants must share the same concept skeleton and runtime truth, differing only in language density and examples.
evidence: The shard defines good Expert/ELI5 differences as phrasing density and assumptions, not substance.
It flags as bad any ELI5 wording that introduces alternate semantics or mutates contract truth.

seeds.title: Close help-system policy gaps in rewrite docs
seeds.statement: Add explicit policy for which concepts require dedicated help entries versus contextual-only hints to prevent inconsistent redefinition across surfaces.
evidence: The shard identifies a contradiction: strong dual-copy contract exists, but concept-help entry policy is not defined.
Candidate fixes call for explicit concept eligibility rules and a dedicated help-entry contract.
